analysis:
Integration of all 23 units. The PR adds an operator-initiated `darkbloom update --rollback` (with `--yes`). It lives in UpdateCommand.swift (validate and run), the new UpdateRollback.swift, SelfUpdater+Rollback.swift, and UpdateRecoveryState and UpdateRecoveryStore changes (rollbackSource, completeRollback without a pending candidate, an optional journal reason). SelfUpdater.now is widened from private to internal. Log strings change in ProviderLoop+AutoUpdate, AutoUpdateController and StartCommand+Modes. Docs, a changelog fragment and the T-043 threat-model mitigation are updated, with new tests.

Security-relevant behavior from the source passes (UpdateRollback.swift lines 64-98, SelfUpdater+Rollback.swift lines 114-117):
- It refuses in cluster and foreground cases and when the installed bundle differs from the recorded release.
- It takes the cross-process update lease with timeout 0.
- It re-plans under the lease and compares the result to the confirmed plan.
- verifyPredecessor checks the tree hash, binary, enclave and metallib hashes and the code signature, with the designated requirement pinned.
- It uses the same journaled UpdateSession.rollback as the watchdog.
- Quarantine is single-slot and exact-version, and it blocks the auto-update paths (a stale v2 watchdog included). Only manualOverride reinstalls.
- The replay guard in finalizeRecovered avoids a double generation bump.
- UpdateCommand rejects `--rollback` combined with `--coordinator`, so no new coordinator trust input appears.
- The new tests use ad-hoc signing, a loopback server and temp roots.

No concrete regression was found. The operator is the same-UID local owner who can already replace the binary (T-013/T-043), so no new privilege boundary exists. A rollback to a revoked or unqualified predecessor would fail App Attest and coordinator authorization (A-016/A-017, T-054, T-057) rather than bypass it. That enforcement is platform-owned and not visible here.

Residual unverified items:
- The implementations of verifyPredecessor, liveMatches and session.release idempotence were reviewed only as summarized in the source passes.
- The predecessor directory's owner-only permissions are unconfirmed.
- Whether T-043 and T-047 need an explicit downgrade note.
- The integration source replay was incomplete (88 units omitted).
I recommend a deeper look at the Swift rollback code paths.
